designationHistory.name: Arctic National Wildlife Range
designationHistory.indexText: Interior Secretary Fred A. Seaton signed Public Land Order 2214, setting aside about 8.9 million acres in northeast Alaska as the Arctic National Wildlife Range to preserve its wildlife, wilderness and recreational values.
designationHistory.note: Signed by the Secretary of the Interior during the Eisenhower administration, not by the President. The CCP gives 8.83 million acres; acreage not rechecked in the order.

sources.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Arctic NWR Revised Comprehensive Conservation Plan, 2015 (ServCat 41955)
Federal Register, Public Land Order 2214 (issue of 1960-12-09)

designationHistory.indexText: The Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act redesignated the range as part of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge and enlarged it.

authority.citation: Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act, Public Law 96-487, sec. 303(2)

designationHistory.note: Range was renamed the William O. Douglas Arctic Wildlife Range in 1980 before ANILCA (CCP; see also Proclamation 4729 on APP); not separately verified.
